*** hcpt CLAUSE RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), refuted by ajcr-p4 (I-1007)
within minutes of my writing it. THE DEGENERACY OBSERVATION IS REAL; MY CAUSAL READING WAS
CONFOUNDED. ***

I wrote, in the self-correction below, that "hcpt is NOT an independent gate but a CONSEQUENCE of
coverage", inferred from hcpt being free at iota := PEmpty while all content sat in the
IsLocallySurjective instance. p4's refutation is decisive and I verified its pivot myself (EXIT=0):
PEmpty IS FINITE. So freeness of hcpt there is explained by the FINITE-INDEX route
(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

WHAT p4 MEASURED, more useful than my claim was: feeding the openCover route directly,
(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

CONSEQUENCE, and it strengthens the item rather than weakening it: DO NOT schedule "derive hcpt
from coverage". The two honest options are the ones the tree names -- a finite atlas, or the Abel
image (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage out of a quasi-compact DivScheme). The class-indexed atlas
needs the second, and PRICING IT is the unowned work. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j points there.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006, after a fresh-context
review of my OWN correction below). THE FOURTH ITEM IS NOT AN ANTECEDENT AT ALL -- IT IS A RIDER
ON antecedent 3, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ARGUED IT. Read this before the arithmetic
correction that follows; that correction's CONCLUSION survives but its UNIT OF PRICING was wrong. ***

WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHAT I GOT WRONG. Right: the count was 3-of-3 where the goal needs more, the
"derived, not assumed" sentence was misleading, and ajcr-p4's discharge is real. WRONG: I priced
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom as a FOURTH INDEPENDENT ANTECEDENT that p4 removed,
and justified its cheapness by the CARRIER the divRep lane happens to return today
(locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom). That argument is CONTINGENT -- it would need re-measuring
if divRep ever returned a different object.

THE UNCONDITIONAL FACT, PROBED, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound]: if divFunctor C pi n is representable by D and by D', and D'.hom is locally of finite
type, then D.hom is. Three lines -- e := rep.uniqueUpToIso rep', e.hom.left is IsIso via
Over.comp_left on hom_inv_id, then rw [<- Over.w e.hom] and infer_instance.

SO hD IS AN INVARIANT OF THE FUNCTOR AT THE PARAMETER, not a property of the chosen carrier. No
producer of rep can choose a D that fails it, and none can be blamed for one that does. The right
place for it on this board is as a RIDER ON THE rep ROW (divrep), not as an item of its own -- a
row that lists it separately INFLATES the antecedent count, which is the same error in the
opposite direction from the one I was correcting.

THE ANTECEDENT LIST OF THE GOAL, corrected again and now on unconditional grounds:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability -- CARRYING hD as a rider that costs its producer nothing.
    OPEN (divrep.u2).
 4. quasiCompact. OPEN, and see the degeneracy note below, which reprices it.

AND A DEGENERACY THAT REPRICES quasiCompact, measured on the same pass. At iota := PEmpty EVERY
explicit input of jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts is free -- hf/hdeg/V/hD/m/Z/nn by PEmpty.elim,
and hcpt free too because an empty family glues to an EMPTY space (IsEmpty => CompactSpace by
inferInstance). ALL the content sits in the single IsLocallySurjective instance. The output is
nevertheless NOT vacuous, and that was also probed (EXIT=0, same axioms): that instance at PEmpty
implies False, because JacobianData.rep yields a point of J over every test (homEquiv.symm 1)
while J.left is empty. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the assembly is sound and falsifiable, so nothing
here is a HasDivFunctor-style vacuity; (b) hcpt is NOT an independent gate of this shape but a
CONSEQUENCE of coverage -- and any future "hcpt discharged" measured at a small atlas measures
nothing at all.

ALSO CORRECTED, and it is a false absolute I repeated from p4's file: "the only declaration in
Picard/ whose conclusion is LocallyOfFiniteType is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom". There are FIVE
non-local ones plus 38 local re-derivations; the omitted ones include the very instance
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199) that Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean imports and cites to make hD free, so the
absolute is refuted by that file's own closing section. THE DEFENSIBLE FORM, which is what a board
row should say: no producer AT A CHART. Same absolute is live on row
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ("exactly ONE declaration") -- narrow it there too.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). THE ANTECEDENT COUNT ON THIS
ROW WAS THREE-OF-THREE WHERE THE GOAL NEEDS FOUR-OF-FOUR, AND ONE SENTENCE BELOW IS MISLEADING
IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. Audited ajcr-p4's finding (I-0967/I-0977); it is CORRECT. ***

THE SENTENCE TO FIX IS MINE. Below, this row says the big-site sheaf condition, the 01JJ gluing
and "BOTH finiteness certificates -- which are DERIVED from chart-level hypotheses, not assumed"
are done and kernel-checked. Read against the statements that is wrong in effect: they are derived
from chart-level hypotheses THAT NOTHING IN THE TREE PRODUCED, which is not the same as derived.
locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (JacobianDataCharts.lean:154) TAKES
hlft : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i); it was, until 67c8d24d5, the only Picard/
declaration concluding LocallyOfFiniteType at a chart, so the certificate was an assumption on
every route. PicRepDatum.lft (PicRepDatum.lean:100) is a structure FIELD -- also an assumption --
and toJacobianData (JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:87) only carries it across. So a lane that
discharged all THREE tracked antecedents would NOT have produced a JacobianData C, which is what
Challenge.lean's frozen Jacobian := (jacobianData C).J actually needs.

NOW DISCHARGED, AND IT IS A REAL DISCHARGE RATHER THAN A RELOCATION -- the part I checked hardest,
because "reduces to X" usually just moves the bill. Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean (ajcr-p4) proves
locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart: at the REAL atlas the certificate follows from
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom alone. And hD is FREE at the carrier the
divisor-representability lane returns: PROBED, imports current, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 --
LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r1 r2 b1 b2).hom closes by inferInstance ALONE at
ARBITRARY window data, via the global instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199), and DivOver (DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:113-116, :308) is an instance of
exactly that shape. So a lane producing rep supplies the fourth antecedent at the same moment at
zero cost.

 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability. OPEN (divrep.u2, ajcr-p3).
 4. hlft, chart finiteness. DISCHARGED at the real atlas, free at the rep carrier.
 5. quasiCompact. OPEN and GENUINELY A-POSTERIORI, and this is the item to watch now that 4 is
    gone. PER-CHART compactness is free at the same carrier (compactSpace_divScheme); CompactSpace
    of the GLUED object is not, and for the class-indexed (infinite) atlas the finite route
    JacobianData.ofCharts is unavailable, so it must come from the Abel image
    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage). Do not let the freeness of the per-chart form be quoted

THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: none of the three OPEN antecedents closes this week (I-0873). Item 4
was never on the list, so removing it does not shorten the critical path; what it does is make
the remaining list the true one. One caveat on the discharging file itself:
Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:65 claims "everything in it other than hf, the local-surjectivity
instance and rep is now discharged", while hcpt is an explicit hypothesis of the same definition
and the file's own :184-186 and :262-265 call it open. The :262 reading is the correct one.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context
review of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.
The route-decision conclusion SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover
`.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed. That step is
FALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on
EVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so "mk at the trivial cover" describes one PRESENTATION, not
the RANGE, and nothing follows about which classes the range contains.

AND THE ABSOLUTE FORM IS REFUTED BY A LANDED THEOREM IN THIS TREE:
PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141) proves the unit SURJECTIVE
over a field test K admitting a curve point sigma, upgraded to a MulEquiv by
PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (:186). Over such tests honesty is DISCHARGED OUTRIGHT -- vacuously
true, no etale cover needed anywhere. So "IsPlusHonest is the sheafification gap asserted of an
arbitrary section" is wrong as an absolute.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, which is narrower and better supported. The gap is at a GENERAL AFFINE BASE
WITH NO SECTION, and the tree documents exactly why:
 * the field route closes only through etale-cover cofinality in finite separable field extensions
   (Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom, EtaleCover.lean:287) -- there is NO
   general-base analogue of that cofinality;
 * EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 states plainly that for a merely quasi-finite (non-finite) etale
   cover the moving statement is FALSE, with a counterexample sketch (B = A_u x A_v over a
   2-dimensional normal local A with nontrivial local class group). So the [Module.Finite A B]
   hypothesis in the effectivity layer is load-bearing, not convenience.

SO THE OBSTRUCTION IS BASE-SHAPE, NOT ARBITRARINESS OF THE CLASS. Two consequences:
 1. the split to hand a prover lane is NOT "chart value (cheap) vs arbitrary section (blocked)" but
    "field test with a section (FREE) vs general sectionless affine base (OPEN)". The delta between
    the chart side and the coverage side is NARROWER than I priced it;
 2. antecedent 2 still owes a route decision -- which site coverage is local for -- because the
    repair still refines covers and descends, and Zariski-local surjectivity still will not absorb
    that. The conclusion stands; cite the module-finiteness counterexample, NOT the trivial-cover
    claim, when repeating it.

*** RANKING AMENDMENT, second reviewer pass 2026-07-29 (run 0082 session 0004, review-ajcr).
ANTECEDENT 2 IS NOT A GEOMETRY BILL, IT IS A SITE DECISION -- so the #2 slot below is
MIS-JUSTIFIED even though its position may be right. Issue I-0920. ***

The costing below is otherwise intact and should be read as it stands. This amendment changes ONE
thing: the reason antecedent 2 (dat-b B-5/B-6, local surjectivity) is expensive.

BELOW IT SAYS: "It carries the content, and its packaging is complete ... What it owes is geometry:
the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation."

MEASURED, tracing the per-point datum through its own producer chain rather than through the rows'
prose. The producer exists (exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range, rooted, sorry-free), and what
it needs reduces to ONE hypothesis: IsPlusHonest (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200). Read as a
statement, that says: for every affine open U of the test, the class restricted to U lies in the
RANGE of relPicToPicEt -- i.e. Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

That is the etale-sheafification gap, structurally:
 * picEt is built on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21), and PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a QUOTIENT
   OVER ALL ETALE COVERS -- elements are PicEtAff.mk E x;
 * PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL
   cover `.self A` alone.
So honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- precisely what the
one-step plus construction exists to permit to FAIL. The tree's only honesty mechanism agrees:

THE ANSWER.  R1 -- varying the pinned pair of P^1-points per cover member, i.e. the p1-aut ->
fibre-avoid -> cert-relocalize chain -- is correct IF AND ONLY IF |P^1(k)| >= n + 2, where n is
the degree, pinned to the genus g by the functor.

Both directions come from one fibrewise reduction (ADDENDUM 4 §4.2).  For c in P^1(k) let W_c be
the image in Spec R of supp D meeting pi^{-1}(c); it is closed because supp D is finite over R,
and s in W_c iff the FIBRE supp(D_s) meets pi^{-1}(c).  Since D_s is finite of degree n over
kappa(s), its image in |P^1| has at most n closed points.
  IF: pick c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines D to the
  chart complementary to pi^{-1}(c).  Doing this at every s gives a Zariski cover on which the
  divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member -- exactly what R1 allows.
  ONLY IF: if the sum over c in P^1(k) of e_c is at most n, where e_c is the minimal degree of a
  closed point of C over c, then a divisor of the form sum_c q_c + padding lies in W_c for EVERY
  c in P^1(k), and no pinned pair confines it.

    change Submodule.Quotient.mk
        (A.thetaSectionsToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j (r • m)) =
      Submodule.Quotient.mk
        ((relResAlgHom C R
          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j)) r •
            A.thetaSectionsToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j m)
    rw [(A.thetaSectionsToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j).map_smulₛₗ]
    rfl

/-- The left quotient restriction as a semilinear map over the corresponding colength
algebra restriction.  This is the left half of the intrinsic theta descent datum. -/
noncomputable def thetaToOverlapLeftColength (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    (i j : D.index) :
    A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a i →ₛₗ[(A.toOvlLeft i j).toRingHom]
      A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j where
  toFun := A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j
  map_add' := (A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j).map_add
  map_smul' := A.thetaToOverlapLeft_smul (π := π) a i j

/-- The right quotient restriction as a semilinear map over the corresponding colength
algebra restriction.  This is the right half of the intrinsic theta descent datum. -/
noncomputable def thetaToOverlapRightColength (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    (i j : D.index) :
    A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j →ₛₗ[(A.toOvlRight i j).toRingHom]
      A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j where
  toFun := A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j
  map_add' := (A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j).map_add
  map_smul' := A.thetaToOverlapRight_smul (π := π) a i j

/-- Evaluation of the widened equalizer algebra on one piece colength algebra. -/
noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraPieceMap (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index) :
    ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) →ₐ[R] A.colength j :=
  (Pi.evalAlgHom R (fun i : D.index => A.colength i) j).comp
    (gluedSubalgebra A).val

/-- A piece theta quotient is a module over the widened equalizer algebra by evaluation on
that piece. -/
@[reducible]
noncomputable def thetaPieceQuotientGluedModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    (j : D.index) :
    Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j) :=
  letI : Module (A.colength j) (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j) :=
    A.thetaPieceQuotientModule (π := π) a j
  Module.compHom (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
    (A.gluedSubalgebraPieceMap j).toRingHom

attribute [local instance] thetaPieceQuotientGluedModule

/-- The intrinsic theta equalizer is stable under the widened equalizer algebra `A_D`. -/
noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedOver (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
    Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) (A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a) where
  carrier := A.intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule (π := π) a
  add_mem' := fun hx hy => (A.intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule (π := π) a).add_mem hx hy
  zero_mem' := (A.intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule (π := π) a).zero_mem
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c x hx
    have hx' := (A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff (π := π) a x).mp hx
    apply (A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff (π := π) a (c • x)).mpr
    intro p
    change A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a p.1 p.2 (c.1 p.1 • x p.1) =
      A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a p.1 p.2 (c.1 p.2 • x p.2)
    rw [A.thetaToOverlapLeft_smul, A.thetaToOverlapRight_smul]
    have hc := (A.mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (c : A.chartProd)).mp c.2
    rw [hc p, hx' p]

/-- The intrinsic globally descended theta restriction as an `A_D`-module. -/
noncomputable abbrev IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) : Type u :=
  ↥(A.intrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a)

    12	# Intrinsic theta descent on a widened divisor cover
    13	
    14	For an arbitrary affine piece `U_j`, the restriction of `O(a Theta)` to the divisor is
    15	the genuine module

    17	`Gamma(U_j, O(a Theta)) / (f_j) Gamma(U_j, O(a Theta))`.

    21	submodule into the symmetric overlap ideal, so the piece quotients have two canonical
    22	overlap maps.  Their equalizer is the intrinsic theta restriction on the widened divisor.
    23

    25	It is the chart-free input for proving invertibility and identifying the result with the

   229	/-- The left restriction sends equation multiples into the symmetric overlap ideal. -/
   230	theorem thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft_vanishing_le (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   231	    (i j : D.index) :
   232	    A.thetaPieceVanishing (π := π) a i ≤
   233	      Submodule.comap (A.thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j)
   234	        (A.thetaOverlapVanishing (π := π) a i j) := by
   235	  change Ideal.span {A.eqn i} •
   236	      (⊤ : Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a i)) ≤
   237	    Submodule.comap (A.thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j)
   238	      (A.ovlIdeal i j •
   239	        (⊤ : Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
   240	          (A.ThetaOverlapSections (π := π) a i j)))
   241	  rw [Submodule.smul_le]
   242	  intro r hr s _
   243	  change A.thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j (r • s) ∈
   244	    A.ovlIdeal i j •
   245	      (⊤ : Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
   246	        (A.ThetaOverlapSections (π := π) a i j))
   247	  rw [(A.thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j).map_smulₛₗ]
   248	  apply Submodule.smul_mem_smul ?_ Submodule.mem_top
   249	  rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hr
   250	  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hr
   251	  rw [map_mul]
   252	  exact Ideal.mul_mem_right _ _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _))

   346	maps. -/

   359	  algebraMap_mem' := by
   360	    intro r

   371	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   372	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩

   385	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>

   432	  have h2 : (s * t) p.2 = s p.2 * t p.2 := rfl

   476	`false`, `t₁ᵃ` on `true`.  The `Bool`-indexed form of `relFiberCoordPow` /
   477	`relFiberCoordOnePow`, which the widened sections need for the same reason
   478	`relThetaResSide` was needed for the twisting unit. -/
   479	noncomputable def relFiberCoordSidePow (n : ℕ) : ∀ b : Bool,
   480	    Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   481	  | false => relFiberCoordPow C R π n
   482	  | true => relFiberCoordOnePow C R π n

   484	@[simp]

   489	@[simp]
   490	lemma relFiberCoordSidePow_true (n : ℕ) :
   491	    relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) n true
   492	      = relFiberCoordOnePow C R π n := rfl

   494	/-- **The widened manufactured section at side `b`**: on each piece, the coordinate power of

   496	
   497	At `b = false` this is `thetaSectionFst` and at `b = true` it is `thetaSectionSnd`, with the
   498	`Sum`-match replaced by a `Bool` comparison against `τ.side j`. -/

   500	  if h : τ.side j = b then
   501	    Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   502	      ((relCurve C R).resHom (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   503	        (h ▸ relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) a (τ.side j)))

   510	          ((relCurve C R).resHom (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   511	            (h ▸ relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) a (τ.side j))) :=
   512	  dif_pos h

   516	    thetaSectionSide A τ a b j = 1 :=
   517	  dif_neg h

     9	# The widened adaptation and certificate (R2, human decision I-0492)
    10	
    11	`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` carries the widened cover datum `AffCoverData` — arbitrary
    12	affine opens, jointly covering, no chart typing.  This file puts the adaptation and the
    13	colength certificate on top of it, clause for clause as in `DivisorFamily.lean`:
    14	
    15	* `AffAdaptation` — equations `f_j` on the pieces plus the point-free refinement clause
    16	  `eqn_rel` (so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms);
    17	* `colength`, `ovlColength`, `deltaLeft`/`deltaRight`, `gluedSubmodule` as a kernel;
    18	* `IsCertified` with (c1)–(c4) unchanged.
    19	
    20	**No clause is added and none is dropped.**  That is the point: consumers of the
    21	*certificate* port by reindexing alone.  What does not survive is the (β2) upgrade from
    22	"inside one piece" to "inside one chart" (`subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` and
    23	`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected`) — that upgrade is the no-go, not a tool, and
    24	nothing here may depend on it.
    25	
    26	The two facts the certificate layer actually uses about a piece are openness (for the
    27	clopen-trace/swallow-or-miss argument, `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean`) and affineness (for
    28	(c1)-finiteness and the localization presentation).  Both are fields of `AffCoverData`, so
    29	the whole per-piece layer transports.
    30	
    31	## Main declarations
    32	
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation` — the widened adaptation.
    34	* `AffAdaptation.ofAnchors` — the anchored constructor (mirrors
    35	  `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`).
    36	* `AffAdaptation.eqn_regular` — the equations are regular, derived not stored.
    37	* `AffAdaptation.gluedSubmodule`, `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff` — the equalizer `W(d)`.
    38	* `AffAdaptation.IsCertified` — (c1)–(c4).
    39	* `AffAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`,
    40	  `flat_colength_of_piece`, and the swallow-or-miss transport lemmas — the per-piece layer,
    41	  proved from openness and affineness only.
    42	-/

    68	
    69	/-- **The adaptation of a local-equation system to a widened cover.** Identical in content to
    70	`DivisorAdaptation` except that the cover datum is an `AffCoverData`: equations on the pieces,
    71	plus the point-free pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel`.
    72	
    73	`eqn_rel` quantifies over ALL `y` — on an empty overlap the section ring is the zero ring and
    74	the clause is trivial — which is what makes it pull back along arbitrary morphisms. -/

    76	    Type u where
    77	  /-- The equation on the piece `j`. -/

    79	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units. -/

    94	/-- **The anchored constructor.** A base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with
    95	`pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)` and a comparison unit; `eqn_rel` is derived by transporting
    96	`d.eqn (pt j)` to `d.eqn y` through `d.ratioUnit`, exactly as in
    97	`DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`. -/
    98	def ofAnchors
    99	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
   100	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
   101	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
   102	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
   103	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))

   107	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by

   109	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=

   111	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   112	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
   113	    rw [map_mul, res_res'] at E1
   114	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
   115	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
   116	    rw [map_mul, res_res', res_res'] at E2
   117	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
   118	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
   119	    rw [Units.val_mul]
   120	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
   121	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   122	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   123	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
   124	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
   125	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
   126	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
   127	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
   128	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
   129	            from rfl]
   130	          exact E1

   132	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   133	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
   134	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   135	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
   136	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   137	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
   138	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
   139	          rw [E2]
   140	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   141	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   142	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   143	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   144	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by

   147	/-- **The equations are regular** — derived from `eqn_rel` at the point itself, not stored. -/
   148	theorem eqn_regular (j : D.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
   149	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   150	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
   151	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
   152	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
   153	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   154	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
   155	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
   156	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
   157	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
   158	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   159	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
   160	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
   161	    exact h
   162	  rw [hgerm]
   163	  exact mul_mem
   164	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   165	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
   166	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))

   168	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
   169	
   170	/-- The piece-local colength module `Γ(pieces j) ⧸ (f_j)`. -/
   171	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : D.index) : Type u :=
   172	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
   173	
   174	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal, generated by both restricted equations. -/
   175	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : D.index) :
   176	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
   177	  Ideal.span
   178	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
   179	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
   180	
   181	/-- The overlap colength module. -/
   182	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : D.index) : Type u :=
   183	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
   184	
   185	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `i` component. -/
   186	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : D.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   187	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
   188	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
   189	    (by
   190	      intro a ha
   191	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   192	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   193	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   194	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   195	          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
   196	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   197	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
   198	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   199	
   200	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `j` component. -/
   201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
   204	    (by
   205	      intro a ha
   206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
   211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
   213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   214	
   215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
   216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
   217	
   218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
   219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
   220	
   221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
   222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   223	  LinearMap.pi
   224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   225	
   226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
   227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   228	  LinearMap.pi
   229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   230	
   231	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`**, spelled as a kernel so the `FlatCokernel`
   232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
   233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   234	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
   235	
   236	/-- The equalizer description of `W(d)`. -/
   237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   238	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   239	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   240	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   241	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   242	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
   243	
   244	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
   245	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
   246	
   247	/-! ### The certificate -/
   248	
   249	/-- **The colength certificate over a widened cover** — clauses (c1)–(c4) verbatim from
   250	`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  Nothing is added and nothing is dropped: the widening
   251	changes where the pieces LIVE, not what the certificate asserts. -/
   252	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
   253	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   254	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
   255	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   256	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
   257	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   258	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
   259	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   260	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
   261	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
   262	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
   263	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
   264	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
   265	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
   266	  flat_coker_diff :
   267	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
   268	
   269	end AffAdaptation
   270	
   271	end AlgebraicGeometry

   584	discipline it owes **two** probes.  "Not silently stronger" is discharged by

   586	the reverse inclusion, the same content as chart-typed.

   588	The mirror risk is **unsatisfiability** — a `Prop` no widened cover can ever satisfy would make
   589	every consumer of it a vacuous theorem, which passes every `sorry` census and axiom probe.  The
   590	probe below rules that out with an unconditional witness, so the residue is genuinely open
   591	rather than false. -/

   594	cocycle is `1`, so every `thetaOvlUnit` is `1`, both spans are the equalizer algebra itself, and
   595	the pairing holds **unconditionally** — for every widened cover, every adaptation and every
   596	chart typing.

   599	which is the open obligation. What it establishes is that `IsThetaPaired` is *satisfiable*, i.e.
   600	that the widened statement is not a reduction to a false hypothesis. -/
